verses.1:
A song. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath Leannoth. + 88:1 Mahalath Leannoth is probably a musical or liturgical term; see also Psalm 53:1|PSA 53:1 . A Maskil + 88:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142. of Heman the Ezrahite.
 O LORD, the God of my salvation,
 day and night I cry out before You.
verses.2:
May my prayer come before You;
 incline Your ear to my cry.
verses.3:
For my soul is full of troubles,
 and my life draws near to Sheol.
verses.4:
I am counted among those descending to the Pit.
 I am like a man without strength.
verses.5:
I am forsaken among the dead,
 like the slain who lie in the grave,
 whom You remember no more,
 who are cut off from Your care.
verses.6:
You have laid me in the lowest Pit,
 in the darkest of the depths.
verses.10:
Do You work wonders for the dead?
 Do departed spirits rise up to praise You?
 Selah
verses.11:
Can Your loving devotion be proclaimed in the grave,
 Your faithfulness in Abaddon + 88:11 Abaddon means Destruction . ?
verses.12:
Will Your wonders be known in the darkness,
 or Your righteousness in the land of oblivion?
verses.13:
But to You, O LORD, I cry for help;
 in the morning my prayer comes before You.
verses.14:
Why, O LORD, do You reject me?
 Why do You hide Your face from me?
verses.15:
From my youth I was afflicted and near death.
 I have borne Your terrors; I am in despair.
verses.16:
Your wrath has swept over me;
 Your terrors have destroyed me.
verses.17:
All day long they engulf me like water;
 they enclose me on every side.
verses.18:
You have removed my beloved and my friend;
 darkness is my closest companion.

metadata.source: Derived from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB). Missing verses restored from the Textus Receptus tradition for completeness.
